visual_identity.core_identity: An oversized beetle with a heavy oval shell and prominent luminous gland structures that make it recognizable even in black-and-white line art.
visual_identity.silhouette: Low oval beetle body, domed wing cases, six stout legs, short antennae, broad head.
visual_identity.head_features: Compact insect head with mandibles, short antennae, and TWO distinct rounded luminous gland bulges above/near the eyes.
visual_identity.body_shape: Three-part insect body with hard domed elytra, six legs, and a compact abdomen.
visual_identity.surface: Large smooth armor plates with restrained segment lines; gland areas outlined clearly rather than shaded.
must_keep: three distinct luminous glands: two near the eyes and one at the rear abdomen
must_avoid: generic beetle with no visible gland structures
more or fewer than six legs
visual_identity.shape_lock: Draw one true beetle with exactly six walking legs, two antennae, domed wing cases, and three unmistakable outlined luminous gland bulges: two by the eyes and one at the rear abdomen. No spider legs, fantasy horns, or extra limbs.
visual_identity.limb_structure: Exactly six insect walking legs attached to the thorax, plus two antennae and mandibles; no extra legs or spiderlike appendages.

accuracy_checks: mine setting benefits from implied glow
no extra fantasy anatomy obscures beetle identity
exactly three outlined luminous gland shapes are visible: two by the eyes and one near the rear abdomen
exactly six walking legs are visible or unambiguously implied

reference.notes: Reference material controls creature identity, anatomy, and silhouette only; Black-Ink controls the final coloring-book rendering style.
